Disclaimer. This site is updated as additional source documents are ingested and reviewed. Its records and calculations are preliminary and open to correction. Additional documents, stakeholder input, and independent review can surface missing information, errors, or context and improve accuracy over time; they may support more complete calculations but do not by themselves verify a record. Inviting people to examine the underlying sources and share corrections is part of the purpose of this work. These are preliminary, document-based observations, not allegations or findings that any person, office, contractor or other entity acted unlawfully. A flag, unmatched record, repeated amount or title, price or location outlier, or missing document is a prompt for review; it does not establish intent, responsibility, benefit, overpayment, duplicate scope or wrongdoing. Names and geographic or district associations indicate possible coverage only, not sponsorship, authorship, control, receipt or personal involvement. Source documents, data completeness, parsing, matching, categories, timing and boundaries may affect results. Verify cited primary records and seek relevant context before drawing or publishing conclusions.

1 · Coordinate review · endpoints over 20 km apart

5 FMR project rows have printed endpoint coordinates more than 20 km apart. Connectivity spatial matching is suppressed for these rows because of the coordinate gap. This is a data-quality review signal; it does not identify which printed coordinate is wrong or establish the actual route alignment.

Method note: the ArcGIS archive contains road line geometry and other road inventory features. The separate road proximity screen compares each printed endpoint with the nearest mapped DPWH national-road centreline (500 m screen); it does not calculate a connected shortest path between project endpoints. These 20 km coordinate-review cases stay suppressed until the printed coordinates are reconciled. A 50 m threshold is used for mapped-cropland proximity, not as a validated route-alignment tolerance.

Conservative FMR allocation per meter

One rate per project: use printed STA length when available; otherwise use the sum of straight-line chords between normalized printed endpoints for each segment. A chord is a lower bound on actual road length if the printed endpoints are correct and belong to that continuous segment, making the resulting allocation per meter a conservative high-side estimate. Coordinate-based values are not measured road costs.

The plot combines two measurement bases but never double-counts projects: 3 printed STA rates take precedence, with coordinate chords for 960 projects. Segments with unresolved coordinates are excluded. Chords under 10 m remain listed for review but are not plotted because very short separations are especially sensitive to coordinate rounding. Sinulatan is included using its printed 0+000–0+479.40 STA range; its single coordinate does not support a separate coordinate-chord estimate.

DA FMR working draft and GEOAGRI proposal records

The November 5 working draft adds 960 control-numbered FMR entries, proposed amounts, coordinate or title revisions, and remarks to the House schedule view. The draft is shown as its own snapshot; it is not treated as enacted or final. Use “Check GEOAGRI” on an entry to search the public proposal API for possible related records.

Interpretation: a matching road name or municipality is a candidate link, not proof that the draft and GEOAGRI records refer to the same project. The November workbook and GEOAGRI have different purposes and evaluation stages. Draft coordinates are kept in the source text; the API result provides estimated length, width, cost, counterpart amount, and WGS 84 geometry.

GEOAGRI FMR proposals · live search

Public GET API, no authentication. Search supports road name, FMR code, region, province, district, municipality, and barangay; status can be filtered. A current list response reported 32,689 proposals on 11 November 2026. Search makes one request when submitted (rate limit: 60 list requests per minute).
